bug_semantics: A backend user granted backend.manage_branding can persist custom_css through Settings -> Customize Backend -> Styles. BrandSetting::compileCss() concatenates that value into LESS input; LESS escape syntax such as .x { content: ~"</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; } preserves attacker-controlled HTML delimiters in the compiled output. modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php places BrandSetting::renderCss() verbatim inside a <style> element from the shared backend head/auth layouts, so the injected </style><script> sequence becomes stored script executed for later backend-page viewers. The prerequisite is trusted backend access with the specific branding permission, but the victim need only load a backend page.
flaw_origin: Commit 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 is the smallest first-writer: in modules/backend/models/BrandSettings.php it changed the LESS parse input from only the bundled custom.less file to that file concatenated with self::get('custom_css'). Its immediate parent already had the settings field, compiler, and style sink, but did not feed custom_css to the parser, so attacker-controlled markup could not reach rendered_css. The same commit also stored compiled CSS for the layout; it is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a move, revert, release carrier, or squash aggregate.
ai_marker: BIC commit object 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 has author and committer Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com> and message 'Cache BrandSettings compiled CSS'; git cat-file -p shows no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: Assigned first-party GHSA-v7cf-8gh9-gxmj / CVE-2026-32257 describes the backend.manage_branding attack and declares winter/wn-backend-module <=1.2.12 affected, 1.2.13 first patched, citing d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720. In the validated clone, `git log --reverse -L '/public static function compileCss/','/^    }/':modules/backend/models/BrandSetting.php` traces the custom_css concatenation to 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74; `git log --all --reverse -S"self::get('custom_css')" -- modules/backend/models/BrandSettings.php modules/backend/models/BrandSetting.php` returns that same sole first-addition commit. `git show 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74` shows the one-line parser change plus compiled-CSS persistence; `git rev-parse 1203043a^` returns fbaab26bfbcfef96bac4802fd6dd62ec5557c8e7; `git show fbaab26bfbcfef96bac4802fd6dd62ec5557c8e7:modules/backend/models/BrandSettings.php` shows parse(File::get(...custom.less)) with no custom_css input, directly proving parent absence. `git cat-file -p 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74` proves one parent and the exact human author/committer/message with no AI trailer. At v1.2.12, `git grep -n -E 'backend\.manage_branding|BrandSetting::renderCss|custom_css' v1.2.12 -- modules/backend/ServiceProvider.php modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php modules/backend/models/BrandSetting.php modules/backend/models/brandsetting/fields.yaml` locates the permission, settings registration, verbatim style sink, and custom_css compiler input; `_head.php` and `auth.php` both render the custom_styles layout partial. `git show d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720` adds strip_tags only to the cache-miss return, and `git tag --contains d28f0...` includes v1.2.13. Direct inspection of v1.2.13 nevertheless shows Cache::forever($cacheKey, $customCss) storing raw compiled attacker text and the early cache-hit branch returning Cache::get($cacheKey) without strip_tags: the first render is sanitized but primes raw cache, and the next backend render remains exploitable. Commit c95d780ab54f3a3f74a94ae1667bf12b3c549d5d changes that early branch to return strip_tags(Cache::get($cacheKey)) and adds cache-hit/pre-existing-cache regression tests using the same LESS </style><script> payload. `git tag --contains c95d780...` begins at v1.2.14; `git diff v1.2.13..v1.2.14 -- modules/backend/models/BrandSetting.php modules/backend/tests/models/BrandSettingTest.php` reproduces the residual-path closure. Thus d28f0... is the advisory's attempted/direct source patch and v1.2.13 boundary, while c95d780... is the actual closing follow-up and v1.2.14 is the first release that sanitizes both cache miss and cache hit.
reasoning: The vulnerable behavior begins only when 1203043a makes administrator-controlled custom_css part of LESS input whose compiled bytes reach the shared backend <style> sink; the earlier 9f5646d2733fc0cd29ecc115c5f2b3fc93ad2d3f commit created the field/compiler framework but left that input disconnected, so it is not the BIC. History -L and -S agree, the immediate parent is directly verified clean, and the BIC is not a squash. AI judgment is restricted to this BIC commit object: it is a conventional human commit with no qualifying AI attribution, so NOT_AI. The advisory-named d28f0 patch is recorded in fix_sha, but because its unsanitized cache-hit branch leaves the same stored-XSS path open in v1.2.13, direct_fix_sha records c95d780 as the true closing change in v1.2.14 rather than overstating the published boundary.
